name: Tivat
title: Tivat Superyacht Hull Thickness Gauging | UTM Refit Support
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Tivat, Montenegro for superyachts and steel yachts in refit: hull plating, tanks, sea chests and pre-purchase condition checks.
h1: Yacht Hull Thickness Gauging in Tivat, Bay of Kotor
intro: Tivat sits in the outer part of the Bay of Kotor and is built around a superyacht marina on the site of a former naval arsenal, with a large yacht repair and refit business beside it. Steel and aluminium yachts come for winter work, and a smaller flow of workboats and passenger craft uses the bay. Atlantis NDT sends ultrasonic technicians from India for gauging jobs, with nobody permanently stationed in Montenegro.

highlights.h: Superyacht refit on a former arsenal
highlights.p: The marina and yard area at Tivat occupy a historic naval site, and large yachts come here for winter maintenance. Hull plating and tank boundaries are gauged once the yacht is lifted or while it stands in a work berth.

Large yachts mix steel hulls with aluminium superstructures, so gauging means two calibrations and a plan for the joints, where dissimilar metals corrode and where plating records are most useful to the surveyor and the captain.

Yacht sales are common in the bay. A buyer's surveyor wants measured plating, tank and rudder-stock data on a yacht before a deal closes, and gauging can be carried out on the day the yacht is hauled.

port.h: Tivat, the marina and the outer Bay of Kotor
p: Tivat is the first sizeable town a ship reaches after entering the Bay of Kotor between the Luštica peninsula and Herceg Novi, on the outer side of the Verige strait. The water here is deep and sheltered, and the bay's mountain backdrop lowers swell to almost nothing. The old Austro-Hungarian and later Yugoslav naval arsenal stood on the waterfront for more than a century, and its docks and quays have been redeveloped as a marina and residential quarter that now serves as a base for superyachts and a shipyard for their refit.

Traffic in Tivat is dominated by yachts rather than merchant ships. Superyachts arrive in the cooler months for maintenance and in spring for charter preparation, and the marina's technical area handles lifting, blasting, painting and engineering work. Between jobs the yachts stay on berths along the quay, where hull and tank condition can be assessed without waiting for a lift. A smaller flow of coastal passenger ships, workboats, pilot boats and small cruise vessels uses the commercial quays elsewhere in the town, and Tivat's airport brings crew and owners in directly.

For gauging, yachts pose different problems from cargo ships. Plating tends to be thinner relative to span, coatings are multi-layered and expensive to strip, and access to tanks is through small openings. Records are asked for by captains, owners' representatives and class surveyors alike, and a pre-purchase condition survey must be finished within the days a buyer's surveyor is on site. A clear plan agreed with the yacht's technical manager before arrival, naming plating panels, tank groups, sea chests and rudder areas, is what keeps each job inside the time available.

The principal gauging place is the marina's repair and refit area. When a yacht is hauled and the hull is dry, the plating, keel, rudder and propulsion appendages can be gauged from the ground or from staging, usually after the old coating has been removed and before new primer goes on. Tank boundaries are measured from inside once the tanks are cleaned and certified. The yard controls access, hot work and lifting, so the technical manager agrees the programme with the yard in advance.

Yachts that are afloat can also be worked on. Alongside in the marina, internal tanks, engine-room bulkheads, deck plating and sea water systems can be gauged without lifting, which makes it practical for pre-purchase checks and for mid-season inspection ahead of a refit decision. For larger commercial ships the bay offers no drydock at Tivat, and owners use the shipyard at Bijela, also in the bay, or yards on the Adriatic coast. Readings taken at Tivat feed those yards' steel estimates.
list: Marina refit and repair area: hull plating, keel, rudder and appendage gauging with the yacht hauled and the hull dry
Yacht work berths on the quay: tank boundary, engine-room bulkhead and deck plating gauging afloat
Marina berths for sale surveys: plating and tank readings for a buyer's surveyor during the days of a pre-purchase inspection
Commercial quays of the town: workboats, pilot boats and small passenger vessels gauged alongside
Outer-bay anchorage: launch-borne condition checks on larger yachts awaiting a berth

context.h: Regulation, flag and class practice for yachts in Tivat
p: Large yachts are mostly regulated through their flag and class rather than through port state control in the way merchant ships are. Many carry class from an IACS society and operate under the code for large commercial yachts, with periodic surveys and thickness records kept in the ship's file. Montenegro is a Paris MoU member and the Maritime Safety Administration is the national authority, but yachts used purely for pleasure have different obligations from cargo ships. Gauging records are nonetheless requested by flag state surveyors and insurers before refit schedules are agreed.

Montenegro is outside the EU, but yachts moving between Tivat and EU ports meet EU rules on the other side, and many are managed from Italy, France or Monaco. Where a yacht holds class, thickness measurements credited to a class survey must be taken by a firm acceptable to that society, so the technical manager should settle this at the planning stage; gauging for owner's decision-making, refit estimates and sales does not carry that requirement. Entry rules for visiting technicians in Montenegro are national and are checked at the start of each job.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Tivat
jobs.p: Tivat work comes in two forms: planned winter refits that take weeks, and short sales or inspection jobs that must be done in a day or two. Both depend on the technical manager's agreement with the yard on access, coating removal and tank cleaning. We settle plating panels, tanks and reporting format in advance, and confirm Montenegrin entry requirements before the technicians travel from India.
list: Full hull plating gauging on a steel superyacht hauled for its refit, taken after coating removal and before repainting
Tank boundary and double-bottom readings on a large yacht with tanks cleaned and gas-free for entry
Pre-purchase gauging for a buyer's surveyor on a yacht alongside the marina quay, covering plating, rudder stock area and sea chests
Aluminium superstructure and hull joint readings on a yacht with mixed-metal construction, taken with the gauge set up for the alloy
Mid-season condition check on a charter yacht to decide the scope of the winter refit before the yard slot is booked

logistics: Tivat Airport is a few minutes from the marina and has seasonal European flights, which makes it the natural arrival point, with Dubrovnik and Podgorica as alternatives by road. Marina security and the yard issue site passes, usually through the yacht's captain or the technical manager, and no commercial ship's agent is involved for yacht work. Because Montenegro sets its own visa rules for Indian citizens, we check them when the enquiry arrives and plan the mobilisation around the lead time.
vessels: Aluminium and composite yachts with steel components

faqs.q: Can you gauge a yacht before the hull is lifted?
faqs.a: Yes, internal structure, tank boundaries, deck plating and some hull areas can be gauged afloat. For full external plating you need the yacht out of the water and the coating removed. We usually recommend a two-stage plan: afloat readings for a pre-refit estimate, then the full hull programme once the yacht is hauled.

faqs.q: Do you measure aluminium as well as steel on yachts?
faqs.a: Yes. Ultrasonic gauges are calibrated for the alloy on a matching reference block, and readings on aluminium are most useful at joints, around fittings and in bilge areas. We agree measurement locations with the technical manager and the surveyor beforehand so the results are comparable at the next survey.

faqs.q: Can gauging be completed within a short pre-purchase window?
faqs.a: Usually, if the scope is agreed before arrival and the yard has tanks open and cleaned. A defined list of plating panels, tank groups and sea chests lets the technicians work through readings in the days a buyer's surveyor is on site. The report is structured so the surveyor can append it to the pre-purchase file.

faqs.q: Is class involvement required for yacht gauging in Tivat?
faqs.a: Only when the readings are to be credited to a class survey. In that case the thickness measurement firm must be acceptable to the yacht's class society. For refit estimates, sales and the owner's own planning, no class involvement is needed, and the technical manager decides how the data will be used.
